subject: LucidHealth — post-call summary, topology proposal & SLO confirmation

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: LucidHealth — post-call summary, topology proposal & SLO confirmation

Hi Craig — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we loop in procurement/security: 

Recap of pain & goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference cost and occasional latency spikes impacting triage workflows (urgent / high priority patient events).
- Goals: 95th/99th latency SLO for short-form inference (under 350 tokens) and cost predictability for production traffic (target < $0.0025/token equivalent for 90% of traffic).
- Data sensitivity: clinical PHI in payloads — Lucid is leaning toward a dedicated/private deployment.

Key technical notes we captured today
- Typical request profile: 70% short prompts (avg 180 tokens), 30% longer generative flows (up to 1.5k tokens).
- Desired P95 latency target: 150–200 ms for short requests in normal mode; P99 < 400 ms.
- Throughput baseline: 200 req/s steady-state, burst to 1k req/s for 10–15 min windows during peak hours.
- Models discussed: evaluation of a 70B-family variant for best quality; fallbacks to a 13B quantized variant for cost-sensitive routes.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common triage prompts is a high priority.

Mutual action items (owners + target dates)
1) Redwood proposal draft + pricing assumptions (attached) — Soojin — 2026-06-08 EOD
2) Topology sketch + SLO runbook (initial) — Karthik — 2026-06-06 noon
3) Security questionnaire + deployment model preference (dedicated vs VPC) — Craig/Sara — 2026-06-10
4) Procurement intro / procurement requirements — Craig to introduce Sara (procurement) on reply — immediate

Attachments referenced: lucid_mop_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), redwood-proposal-draft.pdf (high level pricing & options).

Next suggested call: 30-minute technical run-through (ops + infra) in the next week to validate topology and canary plan. I can hold next Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Craig Muller <craig@lucidhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: LucidHealth — post-call summary, topology proposal & SLO confirmation (technical deep-dive)

Craig / Soojin — following the mutual action plan, attached is an initial technical sketch and a short set of recommendations based on the traffic profile you described. Key points below; see attached topology-sketch.png for a compact diagram.

Topology proposal (high level)- Ingress layer: regional API gateways with request sharding by route (triage_short, triage_long, batch_inference).- Serving clusters: dedicated GPU pools per environment (canary/staging/prod). Use mixed-instance pools: A100/RTX8000 class for prod 70B, T4/RTX5000 for 13B quantized fallbacks.- KV cache & prefix caching: colocate in front of GPUs with warmed shared cache for triage_short route. Cache hit target: 20–30% of tokens for short prompts.- Autoscaling: hybrid steady-state + burst policy. Steady state sized for 200 req/s with scale-in/out thresholds at 60s; burst policy uses additional reserved burst nodes that spin up within 45–60s for predictable burst capacity.

SLOs and measurement- Latency SLOs (prod): P95 <= 180 ms (triage_short); P99 <= 400 ms.- Throughput target: sustain 200 req/s steady; handle 1k req/s bursts for up to 15 minutes with degraded but safe P95 target <= 500 ms using cost-tiered fallbacks.- Observability: token-level breakdown, per-route P95/P99, and trace IDs included in every response for root-cause.

Model and quality recommendations- Primary model: 70B-class (FP16) served with KV cache and optimized kernels for short context.- Secondary fallback: 13B quantized (int8) tuned for throughput.- Routing policy: latency-sensitive routes to 70B; cost-sensitive or background reranks to 13B. Automatic fallback when queue latency exceeds 120 ms.

Operational considerations- Cold-start mitigation: keep a small warm pool for 70B replicas during peak windows.- Security: network isolation, KMS integration for keys, and request-level logging with redaction rules. We will provide SOC2 artifacts during security review.

Attachments: topology-sketch.png (diagram), initial latency/runbook checklist embedded in the proposal PDF referenced by Soojin.

I propose a 30–45 minute infra run-through next Tue where we walk the diagram and confirm canary sizing. Available windows: Tue 2026-06-09 09:00–11:00 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know which works.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
